purpose: Separate two-request cancellation and recovery diagnostic; does not replace, resume, or change the frozen four-turn M7 result.
eligibility: Run a condition once only if its preserved original M7 summary is failed and contains no disconnect-stage check. Passed runs and runs that reached disconnect are ineligible.
session_history: Start a fresh empty main-API session; never seed or copy prior model answers.

disconnect.message: Explain CUDA's developer ecosystem in detail, with several examples.

recovery.message: What is CUDA? Please answer in one short sentence.

identity_scope: Use unchanged parent model/corpus/snapshot/adapter preparation and actual observed_identity checks.
stages: Observe one nonempty disconnect token with the exact provider busy and an empty session context; then close TCP.
Observe provider idle within 60 seconds and unchanged empty session context.
Issue the unchanged recovery prompt once in that session; independently record busy admission, first token, complete result/done, and any raw error or truncation.
Inspect post-recovery session integrity even when recovery truncates or errors; then delete the session and stop both servers.
outcomes: Cancellation transport and memory integrity are separate from recovery admission, token production, and complete response.
A truncated recovery remains incomplete and makes the full diagnostic fail, even if cancellation and cleanup checks pass.
All raw token/error traces and warmup bytes remain private; publish hashes, timings, identities, stage outcomes and actual persistence receipts.
No automatic retry, altered budget, semantic quality score, persona likeness score, or promotion.
persistence: Save success and failure archives with the supervisor owner/log, exact protocol and public summary; freshly retrieve and verify every payload before the next expensive stage.
